claim_text: LALIGA says it was the target of a cyberattack on a fan-services platform
summary: LALIGA's own statement says it suffered a cyberattack aimed at one of its technology platforms for fan services.
detail: The statement is on LALIGA's own website. Reuters (via CNA) and Europa Press report the same statement, so the three count as one source.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's statement says in its own words that it suffered a cyberattack.
notes: Company statement, Tier 1. The two outlets relay it.

claim_text: LALIGA says personal data of registered users was extracted
summary: LALIGA says an attacker extracted personal data of users registered in digital services of LALIGA and of some clubs.
detail: The statement says 'extrajeron datos personales'. It does not say which kinds of personal data. Reuters adds that the extent is yet to be determined.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's statement says personal data was extracted.
notes: Company statement, Tier 1. The two outlets relay it.

claim_text: LALIGA says the attacker had access from Nov 14 to 16 and was blocked on Nov 16
summary: LALIGA says an attacker accessed the platform illegitimately between Nov 14 and 16. On Nov 16 its security teams applied measures to contain the attack, stop the extraction and block the attacker.
detail: Reuters says LALIGA became aware of the attack on Nov 16. The statement does not say how it was spotted. All of this rests on the company's statement.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company states it; no outside source has checked the dates or the containment.
notes: Company statement only; the outlets relay it.

claim_text: LALIGA says the incident was limited to this platform and the competition was not affected
summary: LALIGA says the incident was limited to this one platform and did not affect the rest of its systems or the running of the competition.
detail: This is the company's own finding. The statement says the platform activity is still being analysed to determine the scope.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company states it; no outside source has checked it.
notes: Company statement only. The CNA copy does not repeat this line.

claim_text: LALIGA says it told the data protection agency and filed a police complaint
summary: LALIGA says it notified Spain's data protection agency (AEPD), filed a complaint with the National Police's central cybercrime unit, which is investigating, and informed the affected clubs.
detail: No statement from the agency or the police was found. This rests on LALIGA's statement.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company says it notified them; no agency or police statement was found.

claim_text: How many people were affected and which data
summary: No count of affected users and no list of data types has been published. The statement says only 'personal data'.
detail: Reuters says the extent is yet to be determined and that data from clubs was also affected.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The statement gives no count and no data types.

claim_text: Who was behind it and how they got in
summary: LALIGA calls the attacker a 'cibercriminal' and does not name a group or say how access was gained. We found no claim of responsibility in these sources.
detail: We did not look at leak sites, forums or trackers. Which platform was hit is not named either.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the three sources names an attacker or a method.
